key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current influence penetration, molten-pool flow, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter-dependent trends can guide weld-process optimization for low-thermal-expansion Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Parameter study of laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, higher laser power increased penetration and keyhole size; across 0.5–0.8 m/min, higher speed reduced penetration and weld width; across 150–170 A, higher current widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends within limited parameter ranges but does not quantify simulation accuracy or final weld mechanical performance.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
